searchText: Probably not: disagreements in an OR are rare in that they’re fully specified and completely technical, so they can be adjudicated automatically by code. Introducing coin voting like on Kleros would add centralization risk for no apparent benefit. rollup upgrades are already fully centralized, so any decentralization of that could be beneficial Why are rollup upgrades centralized? Any rollup that can be centrally upgraded I argue is not censorship resistant or trustless at all and should be treated about the same as a centralized side-chain. Or maybe a "beta test" of an *actual* rollup. agreed - they are generally beta-tests of actually rollups i think Fuel is the only rollup that doesn't have centralized upgradability but it's not immediately clear how to decentralize a rollup upgrade process (i think optimistic rollups are the main concern, and possibly optimism is the most concerning because of how tight it's reliance on the exact implementation of the EVM is) You don't. You do migrations. I really wish people would just design for migrations instead of trying to avoid them. how do you migrate optimism? You spin up a new chain that is better and tell people "hey, come play in this new better sandbox". all the L1 assets have to be owned by certain implementation or a proxy Just like Uniswap v1 => Uniswap v2 => Uniswap v3. but you have to have someone turn off optimism v1 because it may no longer be secure after a hard fork There might be mechanisms for building L2=>L2 transfers, which would help reduce the cost of such a migration. Not with a migration strategy. Optimism v1 keeps running forever, just like Uniswap v1. Optimism v2 is a new separate thing that people can *choose* to use if they like. To do so, you migrate to it just like you would migrate from Optimism => Arbitrum. if you don't do that, an evm change may make it possible to submit transitions that can no longer have valid fraud proofs constructed It worries me greatly that people are building these L2 solutions under the assumption that upgradability is a thing they can do. This is a good point, but I don't think in favor of L2 upgradability. Instead, I think this is a point in favor of EVM versioning. some things can't be versioned though, like gas price changes for security We need strong guarantees of EVM opcode stability over time while simultaneously allowing us to iterate on the EVM more freely. L2 proofs should be designed to not be highly dependent on gas costs remaining stable. While I understand that at the extreme there are no guarantees, it is unlikely we'll make the `ADD` opcode cost 5,000,000 gas (as an example). That is, I think as long as the L2 is far enough below the gas limit and isn't doing anything crazy we should be OK. sure, fully agree that the migration strategy is preferable to the upgrade strategy Also, allowing validation to occur across multiple blocks helps. but validation across multiple blocks can blow up the finalization time 😦 Yeah, certainly. We should definitely switch to zkRollups ASAP. 😉 i'm a midwit IIUC, proof generation costs are going down pretty rapidly. Also, my response was mostly tongue in cheek. mine too 😄 Do you think data availability layers help in the process? In which process?
